commands.notes: G3: leaving out the content block keeps the document open and returns it (replaces -NoSave); with a block -Path is required and the file is saved and closed when the block ends. If the block throws, nothing is saved and a partial file is removed. Native save fails on content loss unless -AllowLoss (G4, on Save-OfficePdf). -Font and -Size set the default body font and text size; -FontFamily is merged into -Font and -FontSize becomes -Size, as on every text command. -Alignment parameters take the shared OfficeAlignment. Uses the shared native lifecycle: without Content it returns the live document and writes nothing, retaining an optional associated path. A content block requires Path and publishes only after successful completion; Force is required to replace an existing destination. Native PDF coordinates remain numeric in the target page /UserUnit space.

commands.notes: Replaces Get-OfficePdf. Without a block -Path takes one or more files and returns one live PdfDocument per file (G3). With a content block -Path is a single file: inside the block every command that takes -Document (Add-OfficePdfStamp, Set-OfficePdfPage, Remove-OfficePdfPage, Set-OfficePdfMetadata, Set-OfficePdfFormField, Get-OfficePdfFormField, ...) binds to the open document when -Document is left out, and the result is saved to -OutputPath (or back to -Path) when the block ends; -PassThru returns the file. commands.name: Save-OfficePdf
commands.synopsis: Saves a live PDF document to its own path or a new one.

parameters.name: AllowLoss
parameters.notes: G4: native saves fail on loss unless accepted.

commands.notes: -Path optional: defaults to the path the document was created or opened with. -Open/-Show alias collapses to -Show; -UserPassword alias removed. Uses native output options, so loss is checked before encryption and publication. OwnerPassword alone permits password-free opening with restricted permissions. Security arguments apply to this output without changing the live model; use Protect-OfficeDocument to replace existing encryption. Native security rejects retained PDF/A, PDF/X and electronic-invoice identification.
